LanguageData.CC_Settings_TradeWindow_Tip: Every trade opens in Rimfolk's own window in place of the game's trade screen: a trader or visitor on the map, a guest, a ship called on the comms console, a caravan at a town or met on the road. Two lists, your goods to sell and the trader's to buy: side by side when the window is wide enough, else as two tabs, Sell and Buy (or always one way, chosen above the lists). Each list is grouped by kind, and each good shows its picture and whole name, how many there are, the price with a mark against the usual price for your negotiator, the deal's grade (great, good, fair or poor, in words and bars), what the colony needs of it, and how many to sell or buy. Point at a good for the rest: its market value, the price's share of it, why the deal is called what it is, Vanilla Trading Expanded's market and trend, and what the colony uses it for. Every column header sorts its list, again for the other way. A search, a chip for each kind of good and "only in the deal" above; on the right your silver, the best deals both ways and what the deal comes to; at the foot Fill suggested, Clear suggested, Reset, Accept, Cancel and each side's silver after the trade. The prices, the counts' limits and Accept are the game's own, so other mods' prices and checks still apply. "Game's screen" at the top switches to the game's own screen for the same trade and counts (Trade Helper's panel is drawn there), and a button beside its sort menus comes back. Gifts and trades in favor stay on the game's screen. Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_TradeWindow: Trades open in Rimfolk's own window: two lists, sell and buy, prices against the usual, grades, best deals, a summary.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ToGameTip: Switch to the game's own trade screen for this trade. The counts you set stay as they are, and a button beside its sort menus comes back here. What other mods draw on the game's screen, such as Trade Helper's side panel, shows there.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_BackTip: Rimfolk's trade window for this trade, on the same counts: each price against its market value and the usual price, the deal's grades, the best deals both ways and what the deal comes to.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_GiftsTip: Give gifts to {FACTION} instead of trading, on the game's own screen in its gift mode. As there, the counts set for the trade are cleared.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ChipTip: Show only {LABEL}. Click it again, or All, for everything.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_InDealTip: Show only what is in the deal: in the sell list what is being sold, in the buy list what is being bought.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_NoneToSell: The colony has nothing here to sell.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_NoneToBuy: The trader has nothing to sell.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_NoneShown: Nothing matches the search and the filters.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ListSellTip: The colony's goods within reach of the trade, with what this trader pays for each. Set how many to sell with the arrows or by typing a number.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ListBuyTip: The trader's goods, with what they ask for each. Set how many to buy with the arrows or by typing a number.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ListsTip: How the two lists stand: side by side when the window is wide enough for all their columns, else as two tabs; or always side by side, or always tabs. Kept for the next trade.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ListsNarrow: The window is too narrow for both lists side by side, so they are tabs for now. Widen the window, or make it large, to see both. Click to choose how the lists stand.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ListsOpt_Auto: Side by side when there's room, else tabs
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_SortMenuTip: Sort this list by any of its columns, or by what they leave out: market value, Vanilla Trading Expanded's market and its trend, and mass. Each kind's goods are sorted under its heading.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_NameTip: The good, its picture and its whole name. Point at the picture for what it is, and anywhere else on the row for its whole trade: how many there are, its market value and mass, the price's share of the value and the game's own reckoning, why the deal is called what it is, the market and its trend, and what the colony uses it for. The small button opens its card.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_OursTip: How many the colony has to sell here, as the game counts them: what lies near the trade, or what the caravan carries.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_PayTip: What this trader pays you a piece: the price the trade gives. Under it, its mark against the usual price a trader pays for your negotiator and difficulty (the game's 60% of its worth, moved by them): an arrow up when above it and down when under, and how far, in green when better for you and orange when well worse, "usual" when about the same.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_AskTip: What this trader asks a piece: the price the trade gives. Under it, its mark against the usual price a trader asks for your negotiator and difficulty (the game's 140% of its worth, moved by them): an arrow up when above it and down when under, and how far, in green when better for you and orange when well worse, "usual" when about the same.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_TheirsTip: How many the trader has to sell.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_DealTip: How good the price is: great, good, fair or poor, in words and in bars (three, two, one, none). Read from the price against the usual one: a fifth better is great, 7% better good, within 7% fair, worse poor. Vanilla Trading Expanded's market moves it a step (a good time to sell or buy, or to wait), and so does the colony's own record (better than its best of the last 15 days, or a tenth worse). A purchase the colony has no use for, or a sale of what it is short of or keeps, is never more than fair. Point at the row for why.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_NeedTip: What the colony needs of it, from Rimfolk's advice: short (worth buying), spare (worth selling) or kept for its plans. Point at the row for why.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_KeepTip: Whether to keep some, from Rimfolk's advice: spare (worth selling), kept for the colony's plans (red when this trade sells into it) or short (worth keeping all). Point at the row for why.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_ToSellTip: How many to sell. The arrows point where the goods go: > sells one more, ten with Shift and a hundred with Ctrl, and >> all of it; < takes one back and << none. Or type a number. A good being bought in the other list says so here; click it to take it out of the purchase.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Col_ToBuyTip: How many to buy. The arrows point where the goods go: < buys one more, ten with Shift and a hundred with Ctrl, and << all of it; > puts one back and >> none. Or type a number. A good being sold in the other list says so here; click it to take it out of the sale.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Sorted: Sorted by this. Click again for the other way round.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_NoGradePeople: People are not graded as goods: the game's own price stands.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_OtherBuyingTip: This good is being bought in the other list. A trade either buys a good or sells it, not both: click to take it out of the purchase, then sell it here.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_OtherSellingTip: This good is being sold in the other list. A trade either buys a good or sells it, not both: click to take it out of the sale, then buy it here.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ValueTip: Its market value a piece, with its quality and hit points: {VALUE}.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_PriceTipSell: That is {SHARE}% of its market value ({VALUE}). A trader usually pays {USUAL} for your negotiator and difficulty, so this is {HOW}.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_PriceTipBuy: That is {SHARE}% of its market value ({VALUE}). A trader usually asks {USUAL} for your negotiator and difficulty, so this is {HOW}.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_DealSell: Selling: {GRADE}. They pay {PRICE} a piece; the usual is {USUAL}, so this is {HOW}.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_DealBuy: Buying: {GRADE}. They ask {PRICE} a piece; the usual is {USUAL}, so this is {HOW}.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_RecBetterSold: Better than the colony's best sale of it in the last {DAYS} days, {PRICE} a piece.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_RecWorseSold: The colony got {PRICE} a piece for it in the last {DAYS} days.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_RecBetterBought: Cheaper than the least the colony paid in the last {DAYS} days, {PRICE} a piece.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_RecWorseBought: The colony paid only {PRICE} a piece for it in the last {DAYS} days.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_CappedSell: The colony is short of it, or keeps all it has, so the sale is called no more than fair.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_CappedBuy: The colony has no use for it now (no need, and no stock of it kept), so it is called no more than fair, however cheap.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_DealHow: Great is a fifth better than the usual price, good 7% better, fair within 7% of it, poor worse.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_BestNoneSell: Nothing of the colony's sells notably better than usual here.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_BestNoneBuy: Nothing the colony needs is notably cheaper than usual here.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_BestTip: {GRADE} at {PRICE} a piece: {HOW} the usual price. Click to find it in the list.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_DealEmpty: Nothing in the deal yet. Set counts in the list, or press Fill suggested.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Give: You sell {COUNT}, worth {VALUE} at market value, for {SILVER} ({SHARE} of it).
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_Get: You buy {COUNT}, worth {VALUE} at market value, for {SILVER} ({SHARE} of it).
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_VsUsualBetter: Against the usual prices for your negotiator: about {PCT}% better for you.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_VsUsualWorse: Against the usual prices for your negotiator: about {PCT}% worse for you.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_VsUsualSame: About the usual prices for your negotiator.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_VsUsualTip: What the deal comes to at this trader's prices, against what it would come to at the usual ones (a trader's 60% and 140% of each good's worth, moved by your negotiator and the difficulty), as a share of that.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ByValue: By market value you give {GIVE} and get {GET}.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_ByValueTip: The goods at their market value and the silver as it is, both ways. Trading always gives up some market value, since a trader pays under it and asks over it; the line above says how this trader does against the usual.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_TraderShort: They are {COUNT} silver short of paying it all: on Accept the game asks whether to let the rest go.
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_WalletTitle: Your silver, now and after this trade
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_WalletPay: You can afford it: you pay {COUNT}
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_WalletTheirsShort: The trader has {NOW} and is {COUNT} short of paying you
LanguageData.CC_TradeWin_SilverTip: Each side's silver now and after this trade, as the game counts it. In red or orange where a side runs short.
